transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I guess what made me come in is that over the past year or so I’ve been getting pulled off task really easily. It’s not like I’m trying to be careless or anything, but even a phone buzz, someone walking past my office, or just some random thought—like about my in-laws—can knock me off what I was doing before I really catch it. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you’re asking about, but it’s been happening enough that I figured I should talk to someone.

Can you tell me a bit more about how long these distractions tend to last? For example, if you get pulled off task by a thought or something in the environment, how hard is it for you to get back on track?

Yeah… I mean, usually it’s not hours or anything, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But even a small thing can kind of knock me off for a bit—like my phone buzzing or someone just walking by my office, or I’ll suddenly think about something with my in-laws—and then I’m not on the thing I was doing anymore.

Getting back to it can take a little effort. Sometimes I catch it pretty quick, but other times I have to sort of remind myself, “Okay, what was I doing?” I don’t know if that answers it right, but it feels like I’m getting pulled away before I can really stop it.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be moving or doing something, especially when you’re trying to focus on a task?

Yeah… I do, I think. I don’t want to overstate it, but when I’m supposed to just sit still—like at family dinners or in church volunteer meetings—I get this feeling like there’s a motor running in me. Like I need to move, or at least be doing something with my hands.

I try not to be disruptive or anything, but it’s uncomfortable to just sit there sometimes. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself acting on impulse or doing things without thinking them through, especially in situations where you're expected to wait or take your time?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t think I’m doing anything reckless, but I have noticed I jump in before I really think.

Like with my wife, if she’s talking to her parents, I’ll cut in with what I think is the answer or the point, and then I realize I kind of stepped on the conversation. At work too, sometimes an employee is explaining something and I’ll finish their thought before they’re done. I usually mean it as being helpful or efficient, but I can tell it rubs people the wrong way sometimes.

I’m not proud of that, but… yeah, I think that’s been happening more.

Can you tell me if these issues with getting distracted, feeling restless, and acting impulsively happen in different parts of your life—like at work, at home, and in social situations—or if they tend to happen only in one place, like just at work?

Yeah, it’s not just one place, I don’t think. I mean, I’m still functioning, I’m still getting things done overall, so I don’t want to make it sound like everything’s falling apart.

But it does show up at work and at home. At work, meetings or mentoring conversations can get a little off track because I jump in or lose the thread, and I can tell people get less patient with me sometimes. At home, with family plans or conversations, it can kind of create tension, like my wife maybe doesn’t fully trust that I’m going to stay on top of it or handle it the way I said I would.

So… yeah, I guess it’s in different parts of my life. Maybe not severe, but it’s starting to cost me a little, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any periods where you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had trouble sleeping or changes in your appetite that lasted for several days or more?

Um… not really, no. I mean, I have normal bad days like anybody, where I’m tired or stressed, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had stretches where I’m down most of the day or not enjoying things.

Sleep and appetite… I don’t think there’s been any big change there. At least nothing that’s stood out to me as a pattern. Does that answer what you’re asking?
